title: Low-Rank Adaptation for Critic Learning in Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning
claim: Under bootstrapped off-policy training, low-rank constraints change value error non-monotonically with rank, unlike in static regression where residuals simply converge.
layout: 4 line-plot panels in a row, paired by static vs TD, shared legend
description: Four side-by-side line plots with serif fonts and a light grid. The first two panels show Bellman residual (RMS) against training step, for static regression and for off-policy TD. A dashed black line marks the dense baseline, and viridis-colored curves mark LoRA ranks 1 to 256. In the static panel the residual spikes early, with a higher peak for lower rank, and then drops to near zero. In the TD panel all curves overlap and plateau at about 0.1. The last two panels sweep LoRA rank on the x-axis and plot final true-Q error with error bars. The dashed dense baseline sits inside a grey band. Error is non-monotonic in rank: it peaks at mid ranks in the static case, and low ranks fall below the dense baseline in the TD case. The eye goes first to the colored curves and the peaked rank-sweep markers.
caption: A motivating example: Left: Bellman residual (RMS) over training. Right: Final true-$Q$ error on $d^{\pi}$ vs.\ LoRA rank with 5 seeds; dashed line is the dense baseline.
abstract: Scaling critic capacity is a promising direction for improving off-policy reinforcement learning (RL). However, recent work shows that larger critics are prone to overfitting and instability in replay-based bootstrapped training. In this paper, we propose using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) as a structural regularizer for critic learning from scratch. Our approach freezes randomly initialized base matrices and optimizes only the corresponding low-rank adapters, thereby constraining the learned weight changes to low-rank residuals. We evaluate our method on state-based continuous-control tasks, using SAC with SimbaV2 and BRC on DMC-Hard, and FastTD3 with its SimbaV2 variant on IsaacLab. Empirically, LoRA reduces critic loss during training and improves overall policy performance, achieving the best or competitive results on most tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our low-rank updates provide a simple and effective form of structural regularization for critic learning in off-policy RL.
